footer.headline: Let’s build reliable systems together.

about.headline: I build backend systems that stay dependable beyond the happy path.
paragraphs: I'm an early-career backend software engineer with hands-on production experience building Go microservices, REST APIs, cloud integrations, and operational tooling.

My work spans API and MySQL schema design, query optimization, automated testing, weekly production releases, monitoring, on-call support, and incident investigation. I care about controlled concurrency, recovery, observability, and the engineering details that make services easier to operate.

highlights: Developed production Go microservices with GoFr across cloud-resource management, FinOps, notifications, and observability.
Built Redis-backed asynchronous workers, REST APIs, MySQL workflows, and AWS integrations for production services.
Improved API performance and database efficiency through pagination, indexing, SQL optimization, and batched retrieval that removed N+1-style query patterns.
Wrote unit tests with mocks across multiple services, achieving approximately 70–90% service-level coverage, and added integration tests for critical customer flows.
Executed weekly releases to GCP-hosted Kubernetes workloads, validating pods, startup logs, SQL activity, and service errors after deployment.
Participated in 24-hour on-call rotations and investigated approximately 30+ production issues using Grafana, Prometheus, and OpenObserve.

experiences.company: Data Security Council of India / CID Karnataka
experiences.logoAlt: Data Security Council of India logo
highlights: Contributed to an authorized internal OSINT platform and Telegram-bot workflow for police stakeholders using Python, Django, and MongoDB.
Evaluated and integrated 37 public OSINT APIs across heterogeneous intelligence data while keeping sensitive investigative capabilities access-controlled.
Supported structured intelligence searches and downloadable PDF reporting for approximately 10+ directly engaged police stakeholders.
Received an Appreciation Certificate from the Superintendent of Police, Cybercrime Department, Karnataka.

projects.title: JD Lens
projects.description: Built a browser extension that displays the most useful details from a LinkedIn job post in a floating panel, removing the need to repeatedly expand and scan the full description.
details: Extracts and summarizes the role, company, location, required experience, and preferred skills directly from the active job page.
Presents the information in a compact floating panel so users can evaluate opportunities faster while browsing LinkedIn.
Uses a platform-adapter architecture so support for additional job sites can be added without rewriting the shared parsing and presentation logic.

projects.title: Database-level cost attribution
projects.description: Built a scheduled system that estimated each database's share of a common RDS bill using storage, CPU, and memory weights. It helped a client identify unused databases and contributed to an approximately 70% month-over-month cost reduction.
details: Calculated storage weight from database and index sizes, CPU weight from query-execution time, and memory weight from allocated InnoDB buffer-pool pages.
Pulled utilization and pricing data through AWS CloudWatch and the AWS SDK, then ran the calculation at scheduled intervals with throttling and rate limiting.
Made database-level costs visible so unused resources could be identified and removed, contributing to an approximately 70% month-over-month infrastructure-cost reduction.

projects.title: Sequential transition engine
projects.description: Created restart-resilient Redis workers that preserved one-at-a-time ordering within 100+ resource groups while allowing five workers to process different groups concurrently.
details: Enforced one-at-a-time resource transitions within each group while allowing different groups to progress concurrently.
Used five asynchronous workers and Redis to queue pending work and track completion across more than 100 resource groups.
Made processing restart-resilient by skipping completed resources and resuming the unfinished sequence after application restarts.

projects.title: Multi-channel notification service
projects.description: Built the platform's first end-to-end notification service for Slack, email, Google Chat, and Microsoft Teams, supporting an estimated 25,000 notifications per month.
details: Exposed a common REST API with MySQL-backed email templates and actionable Slack messages for initiating platform operations.
Queued outgoing notifications in Redis and used dedicated workers with throttling and rate limiting to protect downstream services.
Stored failed deliveries and performed one delayed retry approximately ten minutes after the initial failure.

projects.title: Text-to-SQL with T5
projects.description: Fine-tuned a T5 model to translate natural-language questions into basic to moderately complex SQL queries. The research was later published as a technical book chapter.
details: Fine-tuned a T5 transformer model on natural-language and SQL query pairs.
Evaluated generation across basic and moderately complex query structures.
Developed the work into research that was published as a technical book chapter.

projects.title: Price Easy
projects.description: Developed a price-comparison platform that collected and displayed current prices for the same product across multiple e-commerce websites.
details: Used Python and BeautifulSoup to extract current product pricing from multiple e-commerce sources.
Stored structured product data in MongoDB and presented cross-platform prices in one place.
Focused on current-price comparison without claiming unsupported historical price tracking.
